body_markdown:
**DALLAS** (November 23, 2026) — AECOM (NYSE: ACM), the trusted global infrastructure leader, today announced its appointment to provide program management services across three major, multi-year infrastructure programs for the Adani Group in India. With a combined capital investment of approximately $15 billion, the initiatives support a central ambition of the Indian government’s Viksit Bharat vision to transform India into a leading global economy by 2047 while expanding India’s clean energy market and strengthening infrastructure to support long-term growth.


“AECOM brings deep global expertise in program management across the energy and aviation sectors, underpinned by a strong local presence in India,” said Richard Whitehead, chief executive of AECOM’s Europe & India region. “We look forward to supporting Adani Group in delivering these critical programs and accelerating India’s economic growth.


AECOM will act as Program Management Consultant to Adani Group for the development of the 30-gigawatt Khavda Renewable Energy Plant in Gujarat, one of the world’s largest renewable energy programs. The program integrates solar power, wind power and battery energy storage systems (BESS) at an unprecedented scale, supporting the expansion of clean energy generation and contributing to India’s energy transition and decarbonization goals.


The second program is expected to deliver four critical transmission and substation projects across Gujarat and Maharashtra. The projects strengthen the transmission network and help establish a green energy corridor, connecting large-scale renewable generation hubs with high-demand centers, including Mumbai. The program supports greater grid resilience, reliable power transmission and the integration of increasing volumes of renewable energy into the grid.


The third program supports Adani Group’s strategic aviation infrastructure expansion across Ahmedabad, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram, providing program-wide management, coordination and delivery oversight. The program supports the modernization and expansion of airport infrastructure, enhancing passenger capacity and experience, improving regional connectivity and strengthening the airports’ roles as key enablers of economic growth and long-term infrastructure development.


“We’re proud to support Adani Group in delivering these ambitious energy and aviation infrastructure programs,” said Suvojoy Sengupta, Chief Executive of AECOM’s business in India. “Clean energy and improved connectivity will be critical to achieving India’s Viksit Bharat vision, and we look forward to working closely with our client to help bring these transformative projects to life.”


“These programs signify our growing presence and capabilities in India,” said Drew Jeter, chief executive of AECOM’s Program Management global business line. “We are proud to play our part in delivering these transformative programs and look forward to working with Adani Group to help strengthen India’s energy infrastructure, accelerate access to clean and reliable power, enhance connectivity and support sustainable economic growth across the country.”


AECOM has a strong and growing presence across India and is currently supporting some of the country’s most significant infrastructure development programs across renewable energy, water, advanced manufacturing, data centers, transportation, and urban development.


**About AECOM**


AECOM (NYSE: ACM) is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $15.1 billion in fiscal year 2026. Learn more at[aecom.com](http://aecom.com/) .
